current.request: the design misses timing at 200 MHz: improve its timing

options.title: Carry-save accumulator in the multiplier core
options.approach: In montgomery_core, keep the accumulator s as a sum and a carry vector so each of the W iterations needs no full-width carry propagation. This removes the 18-CARRY4 chain from s_reg[1]_replica to s_reg[64]. One carry-propagate addition is done at the end, split across the two extra clocks of the W+2 schedule so the latency stays fixed. The ports, regs and top are not changed.

gain.basis_note: The worst path is 5.59 ns, of which 18 of 20 levels are carry chain, so removing the chain should at least close the 0.615 ns miss. The upper end is a guess because there is no per-level delay breakdown. The final conversion may become the new critical path.

cost.note: This is an arithmetic rewrite. The final conversion must be fitted into the existing two extra clocks, and the new critical path may need more rounds.
cost.basis: iterations are the generator's estimate (a guess); no recorded build time, so no wall-time figure

options.title: Different synthesis and implementation strategy
options.approach: Rerun synthesis and implementation with a timing-oriented strategy, such as performance-explore placement and post-route physical optimisation, without changing the RTL. The 33 failing endpoints and a TNS of -5.987 ns suggest a modest overrun spread over a few paths. Constraints and RTL are not changed.

gain.basis_note: The average violation is about 0.18 ns (5.987/33) against a worst of 0.615 ns. Tool strategy has no recorded result in the analysis, so the range is a guess. It may not close the worst path, which is mostly a carry chain.

cost.note: Each strategy is one full build. Several strategies may need trying.

options.title: Precompute the selected addend in the core
options.approach: In montgomery_core, precompute the operand-dependent addend term (for example B+M) once into a register, so the two LUT3 levels in front of the s_reg adder chain become a single simpler select. The 18-CARRY4 chain stays, so the gain is limited. The precompute must fit inside the existing W+2 schedule. Other components are not changed.

gain.basis_note: 2 of 20 levels on the 5.59 ns path are LUT3, so removing one level might save a few tenths of a ns at most. There is no per-level delay in the analysis, so this is a guess.

cost.note: The change is small but may not close timing alone.
cost.basis: iterations are the generator's estimate (a guess); no recorded build time, so no wall-time figure
